fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Media, Baudrillard and the worldview filter", "body": "Chance cited Jean Baudrillard's Simulacra and Simulation, the book hollowed out on screen in The Matrix, and its line that media shows a world more real than lived reality. He added that a distorted worldview filter makes ordinary daily life feel like the illusion, while TV, video games and cable news feel real because they fit the filter. He and the host traded examples of absorbing characters from shows, with the host citing Jaws and Samantha from Bewitched, and Chance contrasting Tolkien's noble book characters with their Hollywood versions."}, {"title": "Synchronicity as a way of living", "body": "The host described his show as a tale of enjoying survival and a loving guiding force, and Chance agreed that nurture and security let a person function in chaos. Chance described reading events as symbols, the cosmic wink and effortless effort. He said synchronicity ramped up at arts festivals, where he could turn in a random direction and meet the person he wanted to find. The host argued that isolation and shutdowns were aimed at blocking the human connections that synchronicity depends on."}, {"title": "Frequency war and remote biofield tuning", "body": "Chance described sensing a frequency war in festival music, claiming producers embed sigils in the layout of audio tracks, which he gave as one reason he promoted tuning forks and sound healing. The host mentioned crying through the Hannah Montana movie and subsonic sounds in film. Chance said he learned remote biofield tuning from Eileen McKusick's books, explained her map of the field where distance from the body corresponds to age, and said the forks, voice or intention can all find stuck energy."}, {"title": "Simulation as hypocrisy and the language of words", "body": "The title idea came from the host's phrase about the simulation of hypocrisy, and Chance said that in early 1800s dictionaries the two words meant the same thing. He argued that old definitions often show the opposite of today's usage, using for as against: an enemy we oppose is an enemy we support, like two people holding up a wall. He also read utopia as no place, person as persona meaning mask, and a rainbow gathering as a verb rather than a place."}, {"title": "Ego states, touch and a return to innocence", "body": "Chance described Dr. Thomas Zinser's book Soul Centered Healing, which holds that everyone carries ego states created by trauma, separate from full alter personalities, and that integrating them removes phobias and restores repressed traits. He wondered whether tangles in the biofield match those ego states, since energy takes the shape of its container. The host tied healing to human touch, the loss of innocence and isolation, and closed on cuddling. The talk ended with crypto, Govcoin and Webster's 1828 definitions of money and wealth."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Years before NASA showed the moon landing, Star Trek was setting the stage with episodes dealing with The Eugenics Wars and The Return of the Archons. The idea of being placed into a computer simulation or altering your genetics is a tale that runs as far back as the origins of Gnosticism. These thought have been programmed into generations through video games.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: What path can we take to escape the Media-Induced Reality? Where is the balance between the Mystic and the Mechanistic? What cycles of Mysteria has led to the creation of pop icon mind control victims? Are we all Britney now!? The current religion's mindset is "Born this way". Nihilism, atheism, and humanism are the weapons of the 21st century.
